physical.title: painting
physical.summary: Painting on parchment depicting a religious procession of priests of the Ethiopian Church against a yellow background. The priest on the left carries a hand cross and censor. The priest (second left) carries on his head a Tabot which is veiled from view by a canopy of red velvet embroidered with cross motifs. Two other priests wear white shawls with red borders (shamma), one carries a processional cross and a hand cross while the other carries an umbrella. At the head of the procession is a white turbaned priest riding a brown horse. The horse has red leather headgear, crupper, saddle cloth and Ethiopian toe stirrup. The figure mounted on a white horse above the procession is Saint George. He wears a blue cloak (lemd) and a white shamma and carries a spear and gun. The horse has a red saddle cloth and Ethiopian toe stirrup and has a breaststrap, crupper and headgear decorated with silver ornaments which are indicative of the riders' high status. At the top of the painting, in a blue cloud, is a representation of the Holy Spirit.

cultural.vision_reason: This is a classic Ethiopian icon triptych painting showing the Virgin and Child flanked by archangels, with Ethiopian nobility, soldiers, and women in traditional shamma dress below — a well-known Amhara/Ethiopian Orthodox devotional painting style.

physical.title: painting; triptych; religious/ritual equipment
physical.summary:
Triptych comprising three separate wooden boards covered with cotton cloth overlaid with paper depicting scenes from the life of Christ. The central panel (a) depicts Mary and the infant Jesus seated on an elaborate throne flanked by two guardian angels, probably Saint Michael and Saint Gabriel. At bottom left are a troop of Ethiopian soldiers with shields and guns and an Ethiopian noble wearing a white shawl (shamma) with a long curved sword (shotel) holding a rosary. At bottom right is an Ethiopian noblewoman with braided hair surrounded by other women wearing white shamma. These may be the donors of the painting. 

The left panel (b) depicts the crucifixion of Christ and includes images of the skull of Adam at the base of the cross, a man spearing Christ's left side, the two crucified robbers, Mary, John and an equestrian warrior/saint trampling his enemy. 

The right panel (c) depicts the ascension of Christ possibly with the figures of Adam and Eve. Below is the figure of Saint George mounted on a white horse spearing a dragon and saving the maiden Biruwit who is hiding in a tree.

The lower register shows Saint Theodore slaying a serpent. The saint rides a horse with Ethiopian toe stirrup and tack and wears a cape (lemd). A small angel appears to the right.

Verso; Saint Victor is shown slaying a white bull. He rides a horse with Ethiopian toe stirrup, elaborate headgear and breast band. To the top right is an angel.
Framed with a paper mount.

The troops on the left are Ethiopian and are shown full face. The troops to the left are in places reduced to guns with eyes, some wear turbans and shoes with curled toes.

cultural.vision_reason: A traditional Ethiopian devotional painting on cotton depicting the Crucifixion and life of Bishop Selama, in the characteristic Ethiopian Orthodox iconographic style associated with Amhara Christian art.

physical.title: painting
physical.summary:
Painting on cotton, hand-woven in two sections, stitched together centrally top to bottom. The painting depicts the Crucifixion of Jesus Christ and scenes from the life of Bishop Selama. The central image of the painting depicts the crucifixion of Christ, to the left of the cross two angels collect Christ's blood, Christ is offered vinegar on a sponge, his side is pierced with a spear by Longinus who rides a brown horse, the legs of crucified thief are broken. To the right of the cross the legs of the second crucified thief are broken and an angel collects Christ's blood. At the foot of the cross five figures are depicted (l-R) Mary, the Virgin Mary, St. John, Mary and Mary Magdalene. Below Christ's feet is the skull of Adam with Christ's blood falling into his mouth representing man's salvation through the blood of Christ. 

Scenes in the top left corner show the veil of the temple rent in two, the flagellation of Christ by Pilate and Christ wearing the crown of thorns whilst being spat on.

Below (and anticlockwise) are scenes from the life of Bishop Selama; the coronation of Emperor Tewodros II by Selama at Dirasge Maryam Church, Selama being greeted by the priests of Gondar, Selama being expelled from Gonder, Selama greeted by the priests of Tigre, the imprisonment of the Etchege Mahsentu, Goshu Biru, Selama meeting Dejazmach Wube, Selama celebrating communion at the church of Medhane Alam at Adwa, Selama ascending on a rope to Debra Damo monastery.
